This is an engineering default, not a replacement for an installer's design.

data.confirm: I know this system is not recommended and accept it

data_description.control: TPI + PWM: switches the relay in pulses (on for a share of every cycle) by the error and the heat need – fits most relay boilers. PID + PWM: the same pulses with an integral, it does not stay below the target. External thermostat: HC only sets the target of an existing thermostat (a TRV, Better Thermostat, a Wi-Fi heater). AC – virtual i-Feel: HC moves the air conditioner's setpoint so that the room thermometer (not the unit's own sensor) reaches the target. On/off: plain on below / off above the target with long runs (heat pumps). Heating curve: flow temperature by the outdoor temperature.

data_description.reference_entity: Used by fault detection and the shadow comparison. If empty, the relay or thermostat.
data_description.heat_energy_entity: The heat need is learned from these and the temperatures. It needs at least 3 whole days, statistics count too.
data_description.valve_feedback_entity: The central boiler uses it to see whether the valve is really open (on/off, open/closed or at least 20 %). Empty or unavailable: it counts with the actuator opening time.
data_description.floor_entity: The thermometer in the floor. Required for electric floor heating: without it, or without a fresh reading, it does not heat.
data_description.floor_max: No heat above it, whatever the regulator says. 0 = by the covering and the sensor position: under the covering 29 °C for tiles, 27 °C for wood, laminate, vinyl, carpet; in the screed between the pipes 29 / 33 / 31 (vinyl) °C; above a supply pipe 36 °C. An electric floor always uses the under-covering value. Without a covering: 27 °C for an electric floor, 29 °C for a water floor.
data_description.target_source_entity: When someone changes its target (e.g. on the wall thermostat's knob), this instance takes it over as a manual target until the next scheduled change. What HC writes there itself is not taken over.
data_description.hp_defrost_entity: While on (or named defrost), fault detection waits and the run does not count as running without command.
data_description.hp_dhw_entity: A 3-way valve or a mode sensor: while it makes hot water the house waits, this is no fault.
data_description.floor_temper: Comfort: a warm floor. While the room is warm enough the floor is held at the room target + the offset (by the floor sensor); it stops when the room gets this much above its target. The floor limit always wins. Needs a floor sensor.
data_description.floor_fallback: Instead of the blind demand (or, for an electric floor, no heat) the floor is held at the room target + the tempering offset while the room thermometer is silent. Without a floor reading it works as before.
data_description.floor_covering: Gives the floor limit (with the sensor position) and the tempering offset: tiles 2 °C, other coverings 3 °C.
data_description.floor_probe: A sensor deeper in the screed reads warmer than the surface, so its limit is higher. The deeper positions' limits (screed 31–33 °C, above a pipe 36 °C) are estimates: they do not guarantee a surface below 27 °C. Under wood, parquet and laminate a sensor right under the covering (surface) is recommended.
data_description.demand_entity: A dry-contact wall thermostat read through a binary sensor, input boolean or switch: on = heat, off = no heat; then the room thermometer is optional. Frost, window, summer rest, the floor limit and floor tempering still apply. Unavailable: the lost-sensor fallback.
data_description.floor_temper_room_margin: Default 0.5 °C. A larger value gives a warmer floor, but the room swings further above its target and uses more energy.
data_description.extra_factor: Heat per metered unit of the other source: for a heat pump or AC its COP (3 = 1 kWh of power gives 3 kWh of heat).

central.title: Central boiler
central.description: Switches the boiler by the demand of the chosen zone thermostats; waits for actuator valves to open. Starts in shadow mode. With a modulating boiler, the zone asking the most sets the flow by its own curve.

buffer.description: Switches the heat source (pellet, heat pump, electric element) by the tank thermometers: the top below the lower limit starts it, the tank charges up to the upper limit. With zones given a new charge only starts while a zone asks for heat. Starts in shadow mode.

go_live.title: Go live: {name}
go_live.description:
In shadow mode HC calculates and logs what it would do, but switches nothing. Live, it switches the boiler relay (or sets the thermostat / AC unit, the TRV heads) itself.

Go live only when the shadow decisions looked right for a while and nothing else (a wall thermostat, an automation) controls the same output. Every other setting stays as it is.

go_shadow.title: Shadow mode: {name}
go_shadow.description: HC keeps calculating and logging, but switches nothing from now on. The output stays as it is now – switch it by hand if needed.

data_description.valve_feedback_entity: The central boiler uses it to see whether the valve is really open (on/off, open/closed or at least 20 %). Empty or unavailable: it counts with the actuator opening time.
data_description.zone_own_mixer: Off: the flow of a central modulating boiler never goes above the highest flow of this zone (flow_max, 45 °C for a floor by default) while its circuit can get water – radiator zones heat more weakly then. Switch it on only when the floor circuit really has a mixing valve or a temperature limiter.
data_description.valve_exercise: Once a week it opens a long-closed valve for a few minutes so it does not seize. The zone asks for no heat meanwhile, a central boiler does not start.
data_description.floor_entity: The thermometer in the floor. Required for electric floor heating: without it, or without a fresh reading, it does not heat.
data_description.floor_max: No heat above it, whatever the regulator says. 0 = by the covering and the sensor position: under the covering 29 °C for tiles, 27 °C for wood, laminate, vinyl, carpet; in the screed between the pipes 29 / 33 / 31 (vinyl) °C; above a supply pipe 36 °C. An electric floor always uses the under-covering value. Without a covering: 27 °C for an electric floor, 29 °C for a water floor.
data_description.target_source_entity: When someone changes its target (e.g. on the wall thermostat's knob), this instance takes it over as a manual target until the next scheduled change. What HC writes there itself is not taken over.
data_description.hp_defrost_entity: While on (or named defrost), fault detection waits and the run does not count as running without command.
data_description.hp_dhw_entity: A 3-way valve or a mode sensor: while it makes hot water the house waits, this is no fault.
data_description.load_limit_kw: Give the zone's own power in the boiler power field (for electric heat: the heater's). If switching on would exceed the limit, the zone waits and its cycle starts later – the zones heat staggered. Counts in live mode only.
data_description.floor_cooling: In summer (heating season off) the floor cools, but the water and the floor always stay above the dew point + margin, or moisture condenses. No cooling without humidity; on/off control also needs a floor sensor.
data_description.floor_temper: Comfort: a warm floor. While the room is warm enough the floor is held at the room target + the offset (by the floor sensor); it stops when the room gets this much above its target. The floor limit always wins. Needs a floor sensor.
data_description.floor_fallback: Instead of the blind demand (or, for an electric floor, no heat) the floor is held at the room target + the tempering offset while the room thermometer is silent. Without a floor reading it works as before.
data_description.floor_covering: Gives the floor limit (with the sensor position) and the tempering offset: tiles 2 °C, other coverings 3 °C.
data_description.floor_probe: A sensor deeper in the screed reads warmer than the surface, so its limit is higher. The deeper positions' limits (screed 31–33 °C, above a pipe 36 °C) are estimates: they do not guarantee a surface below 27 °C. Under wood, parquet and laminate a sensor right under the covering (surface) is recommended.
data_description.demand_entity: A dry-contact wall thermostat read through a binary sensor, input boolean or switch: on = heat, off = no heat. Frost, window, summer rest, the floor limit and floor tempering still apply. Unavailable: the lost-sensor fallback.
data_description.floor_temper_room_margin: Default 0.5 °C. A larger value gives a warmer floor, but the room swings further above its target and uses more energy.
data_description.pid_d_filter_s: Room sensors report in 0.1 °C steps, only on a change: an unfiltered derivative is spiky. 0 = no filter; only matters when the derivative gain is not 0.
data_description.frozen_after_h: When the room thermometer has shown exactly the same value for this many hours while the heat ran at least the minutes below, the reading counts as frozen and the fallback runs. 0 = off. In the measured house the thermometer stayed unchanged for at most 1.4 h while heating.
data_description.frozen_burn_min: The heat must have run at least this long in the unchanged time: a real room warms by at least one step from that much heat.
data_description.keep_alive_script: When set, at every keep-alive of the relay that should stay on HC runs this script instead of switching the relay on again – for example a Shelly "turn on with a 15-minute flip-back timer". A long burn is then never cut, while a dead Home Assistant leaves the relay on for that long at most.
data_description.adopt_manual: External control: a target set on the managed thermostat itself (not by HC) becomes the manual target until the next scheduled change; if someone switches it off, HC leaves it off (frost protection excepted) until someone switches it on again. Off: HC writes its own target and mode as before.
data_description.control: TPI: proportional pulses by the error and the outdoor temperature. PID: proportional + integral (+ derivative) – removes a lasting offset. Both drive the relay by PWM: on for a share of every cycle.
data_description.cycle_s: PWM cycle: one on + off period. The demand is the share of it the relay is on (50 % of 900 s = 7.5 minutes on).
data_description.min_on_s: Shortest burn: a shorter pulse is skipped or stretched (spares the boiler and the relay).
data_description.pid_kp: How strongly HC answers the error now (0.4 = 40 % demand per °C below the target).
data_description.pid_ki_per_hour: How fast a lasting error adds demand (per °C and hour).
data_description.power_idle_w: Below this the boiler stands by. Leave the defaults (20 W / 115 W) untouched and the boiler health only learns – it judges "no response" / "no flame" by the power draw once you give your boiler's own values.
data_description.power_burn_w: At or above this the burner burns (between the two: only the pump runs).
data_description.extra_factor: Heat per metered unit of the other source: for a heat pump or AC its COP (3 = 1 kWh of power gives 3 kWh of heat).

rooms.title: Rooms
rooms.description:
The rooms of this boiler. The leading room (no regulating TRV head) drives the boiler with the house thermometer; every other room gets its own HC thermostat (climate):
- a room with TRV heads regulates by them: its own target (follows the house target + offset, or its own schedule), optional presence, optional short burns;
- a room without a TRV can only be heated through the boiler: it shows the house target and gets radiator valve advice.

Now:
{rooms_en}<!-- {rooms_hu} -->

The order of the list is the order of the rooms in the HC info house drawing: bottom row first (next to the plant room), left to right, then upwards; with Home Assistant floors the floors give the storeys. Change a room's place in its edit form.

room_remove.title: Remove rooms
room_remove.description: The room's HC thermostat goes too; its TRV heads are left as they are.

room_leading.title: Leading room
room_leading.description: The room whose thermometer runs the boiler (normally the living room, without a TRV head). Its thermometers become the house thermometer.

data.confirm: Yes, the leading room has a TRV head (it gets the house target)

room.title: Room {room}
room.description:
Thermometers: several are averaged (an unavailable one is left out). TRV heads: they get the room's target, calibrated to the room's thermometers (without a thermometer: by their own). Without a TRV head the room follows the house target; the target, presence and demand fields below are then ignored.

Target: "follow" = house target + offset (night, away, presets follow); "own" = its own home / night / away temperatures and night window.

Presence (optional): sensors whose state is this room's area (phone room trackers such as Bermuda, an input_select) or motion / occupancy sensors (on = present). Absent for the given minutes → target − setback (never below the frost limit); household away / vacation → the household target.

data.name: Name
data.demand: May ask the boiler for short burns when far below its target (TRV rooms)
data.position: Place in the list (order in the HC info drawing)

data_description.presence: A room tracker (its state is the room's area, e.g. Bermuda BLE tracking) or a motion / occupancy sensor. Nobody there for the given minutes: the room's target is set back.
